learning_objective: 🎯 Empower yourself! Learn about your legal rights as a buyer, your responsibilities, and how to fight back against unfair trade practices.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: From Consumer point of view: Educates ignorant consumers and protects them from exploitation. From Business point of view: Long-term interest, government intervention, and moral justification.
It protects consumers against defective goods, deficient services, and unfair trade practices. It replaced the older 1986 Act, adding e-commerce rules and stricter penalties.
1. Right to Safety, 2. Right to Information, 3. Right to Choice, 4. Right to be Heard (Representation), 5. Right to seek Redressal, 6. Right to Consumer Education.
Consumers must be aware, buy standardized goods (ISI, Agmark), read labels carefully, ask for a cash memo (proof of purchase), and file a complaint if cheated.
District Commission (claims up to ₹1 Crore), State Commission (claims from ₹1 Crore to ₹10 Crore), and National Commission (claims exceeding ₹10 Crore).

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Label Inspector
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen and pick up any packaged food item. Check for the following: Expiry Date, Ingredients, MRP, and a Quality Mark (like FSSAI). Did the manufacturer fulfill your 'Right to Information'?

exam_tips: 📌 'Right to be Heard' means the consumer has the right to file a complaint. 'Right to seek Redressal' means getting relief (like replacement or refund) after the complaint is heard.
📌 Asking for a Cash Memo is the most important responsibility. Without it, you cannot legally prove you bought the product!
📌 Memorize the financial limits for the District, State, and National commissions under the 2019 Act (up to 1Cr, 1Cr-10Cr, above 10Cr).
quick_recap: ⭐ Only a person who buys goods for personal use is a 'Consumer'. Buying for resale means you are not a consumer under the Act.
⭐ Quality marks include: ISI (electricals), Agmark (agricultural), Hallmark (jewelry), FPO (fruit products).
⭐ The law empowers consumers to form Consumer Organizations and NGOs to protect their rights collectively.
